correctness.rationale: All four update matrices are exact consequences of the stated scalar proximals and probability-weighted extrapolation. P has explicitly positive principal minors and H(0)=I. The exact positive principal minors of H(1/100) and affine dependence on q prove uniform geometric mean-square decay for 0<=q<=1/100. The full-batch reduction has annihilating polynomial B(B+2I)(B-15I/22)=0, and the admitted start has a nonzero (-2)^k component in its primal coordinate. Its event probability q^k proves the claimed bound at every k>=1, including q=1/4. The actual packaged verifier was executed with exact fractions, but the analytic identities, not a finite simulation, establish arbitrary horizons.

value.rationale: The result isolates an objective-motivated failure mode for a published primal-dual method: the same marginal block inclusion rate and expected computational work can give geometric mean-square convergence or even exponential divergence solely through batch coupling. Unlike a minor normalization check, it supplies a robust stable region, an explicit lower bound under independent and coordinated subsets, and rational certificates that are test cases for step-size rules accounting for joint sampling.
